item.title: NBC Western back on air after seven years

item.content:encoded:
Radio coverage in Western Province is set to reach more communities, with NBC Western’s restored broadcast service extending to Morehead, Kondobol, Balimo and Wipim.

NBC Western’s local radio service had been off air since June 2019 after its transmitter was mounted on a Telikom tower that was later decommissioned. The service has now been restored with the transmitter relocated to a PNG Sustainable Development Program (PNGSDP)-owned tower.

The expanded coverage follows a K1.8 million investment by PNGSDP to upgrade FM transmission infrastructure in Daru and install relay equipment in the four remote communities.

PNGSDP Chief Executive Officer Lesieli Taviri said the project took a year of planning and coordination to complete.

“Through an investment of K1.8 million, SDP partnered with NBC to upgrade the FM transmission infrastructure in Daru and install relay equipment on four SDP-owned towers at Morehead, Kondobol, Balimo and Wipim. Delivering this work required careful planning and coordination over one full year,” Ms Taviri said.

She said the partnership combines NBC’s broadcasting mandate and technical expertise with PNGSDP’s investment and delivery support.

Ms Taviri said the agreement also provides for PNGSDP to recover its investment through airtime provided by NBC over several years. The airtime will be used to share information about PNGSDP programs in agriculture, education, health and other areas that support communities.

She said the restored service would also give the Western Provincial Government and other partners another channel to share information with the people.

“The restored service also provides a channel for the Provincial Government and other partners to communicate with our people. SDP is pleased to work with NBC to bring back the Voice of the Sunset to the people of Western Province,” she said.

NBC Managing Director Kora Nou said the resumption of local broadcasting from the Daru station was made possible through the partnership and funding support from PNGSDP.

“Such positive outcomes are the end result of stakeholders working with the NBC to bring broadcast services closer to our people.

“This is a hugely positive development; and I acknowledge the ongoing support of the SDP that has now enabled NBC Western to resume local broadcast from our studio in Daru.

“As much as we try, NBC alone cannot continue to effectively deliver this important national service; we need all key stakeholders to partner with us,” Mr Nou said.

Mr Nou also highlighted the importance of reliable communication during the prevailing El Niño conditions.

“With the effects of El Niño being felt in communities, access to timely and reliable information is critical. NBC’s provincial stations play an important role in communicating public advisories and emergency information, helping communities stay informed and prepared,” he said.

He said strong provincial broadcasting services would also be important ahead of the 2027 National General Elections.

“As we prepare for the 2027 general elections, strong provincial broadcasting services will again be crucial in ensuring people have access to public information, civic education, and election-related awareness,” Mr Nou said.

Meanwhile, NBC’s 95.5 FM signal reaches as far as Kiunga, Tabubil, Ningerum, Telefomin and Olsobip. The signal is also received across the Torres Strait Islands, including Saibai, Boigu, Dauan and Stephen Island, as well as coastal villages extending to Bula.

item.title: East New Britain residents urged to report El Nino impacts
item.description: The public in East New Britain has been urged to report all El Niño-related incidents to their respective District Administrators. The District Administrators are heading emergency centres established in the province’s four districts and are responsible for relaying reports to the Provincial Emergency Operating Centre [PEOC] in Kokopo.
item.content:encoded:
The public in East New Britain has been urged to report all El Niño-related incidents to their respective District Administrators.

The District Administrators are heading emergency centres established in the province’s four districts and are responsible for relaying reports to the Provincial Emergency Operating Centre [PEOC] in Kokopo.

Provincial Administrator and Provincial Disaster Committee Chairman Levi Mano said the PEOC, located at the Disaster Office at Kokopo Fire Station, had been activated recently to coordinate the province’s El Niño response.

He said the centre would work with relevant emergency service providers, including ambulance services, fire services and security forces, to ensure appropriate responses to reported incidents.

However, most response activities will be carried out by the respective district administrations, the National Disaster Centre and the National Treasury Department.

Meanwhile, ward recorders have been tasked with completing a standardised reporting form to monitor the effects of El Niño on water supplies, food availability and community health.

The Ward El Niño Drought Water and Food Daily Assessment Format is designed to provide daily information on conditions in affected communities, helping authorities plan responses and allocate resources where they are needed.

At a meeting held at the PEOC last week, District Administrators and Local Level Government [LLG] Managers submitted updated data on affected households and populations across their respective wards and LLGs.

Deputy Provincial Administrator Danley Puapena said some wards were yet to submit their updated information.

“Our technical team will update and get us through the baseline data we have so that the budget and program for K2.5 million at each district is framed and allocated according to baseline data we have to date,” Mr Puapena said.

The PEOC stressed that accurate and reliable data was essential before relief assistance could be distributed.

Without verified information, the province would struggle to effectively deploy water trucks, distribute food rations and provide medical assistance to affected communities.

item.title: ​MMDDA advances rural electrification drive across Mendi-Munihu district
item.description: Mendi-Munihu District Development Authority (MMDDA) continues to expand power grid connectivity to remote communities across the district. ​Local MP and MMDDA Chairman, Raphael Tonpi announced that people in Heyep, Posulim, and Oleya communities will soon be integrated into the main power grid. This follows the successful electrification of the Wambip, Tulum, and Wei villages in earlier phases of
item.content:encoded:
Mendi-Munihu District Development Authority (MMDDA) continues to expand power grid connectivity to remote communities across the district.

​Local MP and MMDDA Chairman, Raphael Tonpi announced that people in Heyep, Posulim, and Oleya communities will soon be integrated into the main power grid. This follows the successful electrification of the Wambip, Tulum, and Wei villages in earlier phases of the rollout.

​“Connecting one village at a time is the most effective way forward,” MP Tonpi stated, reaffirming the MMDDA's systematic approach to delivering vital utilities to rural households.

​He said the ongoing electrification initiative is being delivered through a partnership involving the MMDDA, the Southern Highlands Provincial Government, Kumul Petroleum Holdings Limited (KPHL), and the Japan International Cooperation System (JICS).

In a parallel effort supported by the Japanese Government, 500 households in Mendi-Munihu were recently connected through a joint venture between the MMDDA and the JICS.

MP Tonpi revealed that grid extension work will expand deeper into remote areas. Planned targets include the Pingirip and Sengso communities within the Bush Karinz area, as well as the stretch from the Injed turn-off to Bim mountain along the Southern Highlands–Enga border.

He stressed that connections are also planned for Penrenz Hiri near the Hela Province boundary.

​“Our goal is simple: we want all our people to have access to electricity,” Tonpi emphasized.

The MP emphasized that reliable electricity will serve as a catalyst for local economic development. It is expected to stimulate Small to Medium Enterprises (SMEs), unlock new income-generating opportunities, and boost household livelihoods across the district.

"​Furthermore, access to power will significantly improve public service delivery. Schools will be able to utilize modern educational technologies and upgraded facilities, while rural health centers will gain the capability to deliver continuous, 24/7 medical care," he said.

He encourage the people of Mendi-Munihu to safeguard these vital public assets and leverage the access to power to elevate our standard of living.

item.title: Hela receives 1.5 mw solar power station gift from China government
item.description: Hela Governor Philip Undialu has expressed gratitude to the Government of the People’s Republic of China and His Excellency Ambassador Yang Xiaoguang for gifting a 1.5-megawatt solar power station to Hela province on Sunday. The new facility, located at Hope Institute in Tari, was officially launched in a ceremony witnessed by Prime Minister James Marape and Komo-Hulia MP Daniel Tindipu.
item.content:encoded:
Hela Governor Philip Undialu has expressed gratitude to the Government of the People’s Republic of China and His Excellency Ambassador Yang Xiaoguang for gifting a 1.5-megawatt solar power station to Hela province on Sunday.

The new facility, located at Hope Institute in Tari, was officially launched in a ceremony witnessed by Prime Minister James Marape and Komo-Hulia MP Daniel Tindipu.

Governor Undialu says the project will drive to secure reliable and sustainable electricity for education, health, business and other essential services.

“Tari township has traditionally received only four to six hours of electricity daily from PNG Power. Hela has supplied power to Porgera since 1992 and contributed to global energy supplies through PNG LNG since 2014, yet our own people have continued to experience unreliable electricity. Today, we are changing that reality,” Governor Undialu said.

He said the new 1.5MW solar station at Hope Institute adds to other power initiatives in the province, including a 1MW solar project at Yangome funded by the Provincial Government with support from the National Government through Kumul Consolidated Holdings (KCH), and 2MW gas-fired power stations built by ExxonMobil.

The Governor also announced plans for a major expansion, revealing a proposal for a new 15MW solar power project and welcoming Chinese investment and partnership to make it a reality.

“China is a major consumer of LNG, of which 86 percent comes from Hela. I therefore welcome the Chinese Government and investors to partner with us in future solar and hydroelectricity projects to offset carbon emissions, expand clean energy, create economic opportunities and improve services for our people,” he said.

He said access to reliable 24-hour power will enable Hope Institute to expand its educational programs and services.

He further announced that the Hela Provincial Government has made a submission to the State, through PNG Power Limited, to take over Hela operations under the Government’s plan to sell off B and C-Centres. Once that process is completed, he said, the Provincial Government is committed to working towards reducing electricity tariffs by 50 percent.

Governor Undialu called on local communities to take ownership and protect the new solar facility so that it continues to benefit current and future generations.

“Our vision is a Hela where our schools, hospitals and businesses have cheap, reliable electricity, and our people enjoy the benefits of our resources,” Governor Undialu said.

item.title: Rabaul residents get free water as dry season continues
item.description: Residents in Rabaul District can now access free clean water from two new public outlets established through a partnership between the Rabaul District Administration and Water PNG Limited. The outlets are located at Kaivuna, Ward 4 of Rabaul Urban LLG, along the Matupit-SSM Road, and at Nonga village in front of the Balanataman LLG office complex.
item.content:encoded:
Residents in Rabaul District can now access free clean water from two new public outlets established through a partnership between the Rabaul District Administration and Water PNG Limited.

The outlets are located at Kaivuna, Ward 4 of Rabaul Urban LLG, along the Matupit-SSM Road, and at Nonga village in front of the Balanataman LLG office complex.

The initiative comes as communities face a prolonged dry season, with the new facilities expected to ease access to water for households in the surrounding areas.

Under a three-year partnership agreement, Water PNG is providing access to its existing water infrastructure, while the district administration will pay the monthly water bills, allowing the public to collect water free of charge.

Both outlets are open daily from 8am to 6pm.

Rabaul District Administrator Freddy Lemeki said access to clean water was essential during the prolonged dry season and thanked Water PNG management for supporting the initiative.

“Water is essential, and we thank the Water PNG management for their understanding and willingness to partner with us using their existing water supply systems to set up taps for public use,” Mr Lemeki said.

The Kaivuna outlet will serve residents in Rabaul town, the Matupit and SSM corridors, and nearby communities.

The Nonga outlet will provide water to residents of Nonga, Tavui and other communities along the Balanataman and Kabiu LLG areas.

With the two new outlets, Rabaul District now has three free public water supply points, including the existing facility at the district headquarters in Kurakakaul.

Mr Lemeki said work was also underway to refurbish two water bores owned by Coconut Products Limited [CPL] to supply water to the Malaguna No. 2 Ward Hall.

He urged communities to look after the new facilities, adding that tracking sheets would be maintained at each site to monitor usage and support evaluation.

Water PNG Team Leader for Water Production, Mohu Moana, commended the district administration for the partnership and reaffirmed the company’s commitment to working with local authorities to improve service delivery.

item.title: GPHA nurses end emergency and critical care training

item.content:encoded:
Nurses from the Gulf Provincial Health Authority (GPHA) can now assess and treat patients efficiently based on the severity of their illness following a two-week Emergency and Critical Care Training that ended in Kerema last week.

The training introduced and implemented the Interagency Integrated Triage Tool (ITT) system at the hospital. Through the system, nurses learnt how to identify critically ill and severe trauma cases and also prioritize care.

Facilitator of the training, emergency physician Dr. Ovia Bue, said the training in Gulf differed from trainings he had run in other provinces because nurses at Kerema General lacked background knowledge on emergency cases, and the training had to be done from ground level up.

Despite that, Dr. Bue said participants showed eagerness to learn and grasped all information given to them through the training.

He said the training also helped identify exceptional nurses who can stand in to assist emergency patients in the absence of a doctor or Health Extension Officer on the ground.

Dr. Bue has requested continuous visitation by emergency physicians to Kerema to ensure the knowledge and skills gained are upkept.

Participant Representative Wanpis Epeol said for the last years, Kerema General Hospital has not had an emergency department and has seen patients as they come.

Epeol said because there are no urban clinics in Kerema, the General Hospital has become the urban clinic, which has removed the focus of emergency care.

He said for many years no trainings have been given to emergency nurses on how to care for severely ill patients until now, when training was given by emergency doctors.

"With the triage system in place, we can now assess the patients efficiently and attend to those that need urgent attention," Mr Epeol said.

He also called for the same training to be extended to health workers at the rural health stations.

The Australian High Commission in a statement says, Jamie Isbister has been appointed as PNG’s High Commissioner designate, and he will remain as such, until he presents his credentials to the Governor General of PNG, to assume his officia
item.content:encoded:
A new Australian High Commissioner, has been sent to Papua New Guinea, following the completion of Ewen McDonald’s tenure, as Australia’s representative to PNG.

The Australian High Commission in a statement says, Jamie Isbister has been appointed as PNG’s High Commissioner designate, and he will remain as such, until he presents his credentials to the Governor General of PNG, to assume his official role.

The High Commission says that Mr. Isbister’s appointment is important, because it comes during a period of close ties between the two countries, which is strengthened by the Pukpuk Alliance, bilateral partnership.

It also says that Mr. Isbister brings with him more than 30 years of experience in foreign, humanitarian, and development policy, and he was also the lead negotiator, with the Australian Rugby League Commission, regarding the PNG Chief’s entry into the NRL.

Meanwhile, Mr. Isbister said that he is honoured to be appointed to the post, because his very first memory of life was of Port Moresby, where his father was working as a doctor, at the Port Moresby General Hospital.

item.title: RCPNG to celebrate 40 years of ministry in East Sepik
item.description: Revival Center of PNG (RCPNG) will celebrate 40 years of ministry in East Sepik Province with a four-day anniversary celebration in Wewak, beginning on Thursday, October 29, 2026. The church was established in East Sepik on November 1, 1986, by its Founder and Principal Pastor, Godfrey Wippon with November 1 this year marking four decades of ministry in the province.
item.content:encoded:
Revival Center of PNG (RCPNG) will celebrate 40 years of ministry in East Sepik Province with a four-day anniversary celebration in Wewak, beginning on Thursday, October 29, 2026.

The church was established in East Sepik on November 1, 1986, by its Founder and Principal Pastor, Godfrey Wippon with November 1 this year marking four decades of ministry in the province.

Momase Regional Pastor Collinson Solmen says preparations are progressing, with church members and visitors already arriving in Wewak from across the province and other parts of the country.

“Currently, we have 300 people already on the ground, coming from the six districts and other provinces,” Pastor Solmen said.

He said organisers are anticipating a significant turnout, with between 5,000 and 10,000 people expected to travel to Wewak for the anniversary.

The celebrations will begin on Thursday with a float procession through Wewak town, culminating at King Charles Oval at Kaltex, where Pastor Wippon will officially open the four-day programme.

Pastor Solmen has extended an open invitation to Christians from all denominations and members of the public to participate in the milestone event.

He is encouraging people from different churches and communities to come together in fellowship as the Revival Centre reflects on its 40-year journey and ministry in East Sepik Province.

The anniversary programme will conclude on Sunday, November 1, the exact date the church marks 40 years since its establishment in the province.
